one_month_reasoning: Main event in the window: Q3 2026 results, projected for about Nov 3-4, 2026 (not yet confirmed; Q3 2025 reported Nov 4 and Q2 2026 Aug 5, both before the open), so the reaction most likely lands on or just before the Nov 4 scoring date. Guidance is GB $58.25-60.25B and non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 against about $0.87 consensus. Base rate: Uber's average absolute earnings-day move is about 5.8%, and 6 of the last 8 were negative (Q1 2026 was +8.5% on the day after). With the stock near its 52-week low and sentiment already washed out, I don't call a direction. The Delivery Hero offer acceptance window ends Nov 5, just outside the window. I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median $69.9 (barely above spot) and 11% one-month sigma: normal monthly vol is 35%/3.5 = 10%, and I add a little for earnings.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, all valued on forward numbers as of Oct 2027: P/E (forward EPS of about $4.78 after a 10% haircut x 17x = $81), EV/EBITDA (forward adj. EBITDA of $14.2B x 11x, net debt about 0, 2.0B shares = $78), and FCF yield (forward FCF $12.5B / 7.5% = $83). Weights 0.4/0.3/0.3.

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener 2028E $5.79, rounded down for staleness of that table
2026 EPS consensus was cut from $4.15 to $3.30 in early 2026 on AV spend; the >$10B AV investment plan still carries estimate-cut risk

Peer median fwd P/E is 20.3x (range 8-40x). Uber trades at 16.8x today. I use 17x, below the median, because Lyft, the closest ride-hail peer, sits at 8x and AV disintermediation risk (Waymo leaving the Phoenix/Austin/Atlanta exclusivity) argues against a peer-median re-rating within 12 months

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at Oct-2027 = 0.25x$13.8B + 0.75x$16.5B = $15.8B, haircut 10% = $14.2B; x11x = $156B EV; net debt about 0 excluding Delivery Hero; 2.0B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener EBITDA estimates; 2026E $11.4B is consistent with Q2 $2.82B and Q3 guide $2.86-2.96B

Peer median about 14.7x on a mixed fwd/trailing basis (range 4-32x). Uber's adjusted EBITDA excludes stock comp, so I apply a discount to 11x, near BKNG/EXPE and close to Uber's own MarketScreener 2027E of about 9.7x at $68

Net debt today is $4.7B (debt $12.7B, cash $5.4B plus investments). About $10B+ of annual FCF less buybacks (H1 2026 $3.5B) brings net debt to about zero. Diluted shares are 2.05B, trending lower on buybacks. Delivery Hero (closes H2 2027) is treated as value-neutral: debt-funded, with acquired EBITDA offsetting it

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Oct-2027 about $12.5B / 7.5% yield = $167B / 2.0B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener implies about $13.8B of 2027 FCF (9.71% yield at $141.7B market cap). I haircut it for AV fleet investment
Uber's current yield is about 7.1% (TTM FCF/market cap) and TIKR cites 8.4%. I assume no re-rating, so the market's AV discount persists

bear.story: Waymo/Tesla scale (Waymo targeting 1M+ weekly rides, more cities) and AV-disintermediation fears deepen. A 2027 recession hits (Kalshi prices about 39% for two negative quarters through Q4 2027), consensus EPS is cut 10-15%, and the multiple compresses toward Lyft-like levels of about 12x.

base.story: Gross bookings keep growing high-teens, EPS tracks about $4.4-4.5 for 2027 and buybacks continue. The AV overhang caps the multiple near 15-16x NTM. The usual large-cap partial mean reversion after a 30% drawdown pulls the price modestly above spot.

bull.story: The aggregator thesis gets evidence: AV partners (120k+ vehicles, 15 partners) ramp on the platform, Delivery Hero closes accretively, and the multiple re-rates to about 19-20x NTM EPS of about $5.3, back toward the $101 52-week high.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I claim no premium. The discount reflects two things that should last through the horizon: (1) Lyft, the closest same-business peer, trades at 8x, showing the market applies a structural AV-disruption discount to ride-hail; (2) Waymo ending exclusivity (Phoenix ended May 2026, Austin/Atlanta app Jan 2028) keeps that risk live. Uber's adjusted EBITDA also excludes stock comp, which justifies a lower EBITDA multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $54 is about 22% below spot and about 17% below the $65.41 52-week low, roughly 12x 2027E EPS. Trading there would most likely mean earnings expectations are being cut (bookings growth falling to low-teens, a recession-driven trip slowdown, or AV players visibly taking share in core US cities), not ordinary 35%-vol noise.

reasoning: I start from base rates. A typical large cap moves +/-25-35% in a year, and UBER's realized vol is 35%. The stock has fallen 29.5% in a year and sits near its $65.41 low. It has had worse drawdowns before (-68% in 2021-22, then +149% in 2023), so mean reversion from washed-out levels is real, but so is 12-month loser momentum. On fundamentals, the trend is still strong: Q2 2026 gross bookings were +24%, adj. EBITDA +33%, TTM FCF topped $10B, and the Q3 guide implies EPS growth of +28-35%. The narrative is weak. The Q3 guide was slightly light, there is a >$10B AV spend, Waymo is ending exclusivity, and Delivery Hero adds debt. The market prices about 16.8x forward EPS, below the 20.3x median of a 10-company peer set but well above Lyft at 8x. My blended fair value is about $80 (P/E $81, EV/EBITDA $78, FCF yield $83), roughly 15% above spot. I assume only part of that gap closes because the AV discount looks persistent. For the distribution I use a mixture: 80% weight on a lognormal with median $77 and sigma 0.30 (fundamentals path), 20% on a stress lognormal with median $52 and sigma 0.32 (AV disruption and/or 2027 recession; Kalshi 2027 recession about 39%, partly reflected). The mixture median is about $72 with a fat left tail. Probabilities: about 54% for >= $70, 13% for >= $104, 14% for < $49. Limits: Twelve Data fundamentals endpoints were unavailable on this plan. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is partly trailing or stale (MarketScreener tables dated Feb 2026). I did not use options data.
